_comment: A vanilla swap valued by the captive engine — the first QuantLib warrant this platform can actually execute rather than describe. Everything the valuation reads is in this document: the evaluation date, the curve, and the one past fixing the first floating period needs. Nothing is fetched, because a number fetched at run time is a number nobody can reconcile afterwards.

operation.note: T0: the parameter object is terminal. There is nothing to fit — the constants come from theory and the inputs come from the curve — so law L-W1 refuses a fit warrant for this model, and that refusal is the class working rather than a limitation.

inputs.name: market
inputs.description: The evaluation date is here and not taken from the clock: a valuation that reads today is not reproducible tomorrow, and a backtest of it is a backtest of nothing. The fixing is here for the same reason — the first floating period began before the evaluation date, and a valuation that invented that fixing would put an unversioned number into a governed computation.

assumptions: EUR swaps against a six-month floating index
Maturities out to ten years; the curve's last pillar is 2036 and beyond it the engine extrapolates flat, which is a stated convention rather than a fact about the market
No collateral or funding adjustment: this is a discounting valuation, not an XVA
